name: Aardwolf Shop
author: Solao
description: Shop stock in a panel. Click a name to appraise it, a number to buy that many.
script:
--[[ aw-shop.lua Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-05 'list' in a shop, copied into a panel as rows you can click to buy from. The MUD's own list still scrolls past in the main window — this is an extra, and the extra is that the rows are buttons. What it reads: Num Level Price Qty Item --- ----- ------- --- ----------------------------------- 1 5 20 --- [Potion] Optical Precision 7 69 625 1 (Polished) plain tunic Quantity '---' means unlimited supply. Fixed width, and the Num column is the whole point: Aardwolf's 'buy' takes that number, so a row can be a button without guessing at keywords the way the hunt links have to. Qty is '---' for unlimited or a count for limited stock, and a sold-out line simply isn't listed. One press, one command. Clicking a row's number sends 'buy ' and nothing else — no confirm dialog, but also no chaining into wearing or wielding it. Same line the S&D panel draws: the client saves you typing, it doesn't play for you. Prices are not checked against your gold. The MUD already says no better than we could, and a client that greys out what it thinks you can't afford is wrong the moment you sell something. Ported from the Mudlet shopwin module. Two things changed for this client and both are noted where they happen: colour comes off the line through parseAnsiText into generated CSS classes because the widget sanitiser drops inline colour, and the pager is gone because a div scrolls. ]] plugin = { id = "aw-shop", name = "Aardwolf Shop", version = "1.0.1", author = "Solao", description = "Shop stock in a panel. Click a name to appraise it, a number to buy that many.", settings = { saveState = true }, } -- @category widgets local TAG = "$Y[Shop v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w " local VAR = "aw_shop_cfg" --[[ Aardwolf's buy takes a count: 'buy 20 2' is twenty of item 2. Presets rather than a stepper you click twenty times, and per row rather than a quantity setting that persists — a number remembered from the last purchase is the kind of state that empties your gold when you forget it's set. A button is one click and there is no confirmation, so the biggest one on screen should still be a quantity you could mean. 1000 of a 9,300 gold item is nine million; a fat-fingered extra zero shouldn't be reachable in one press. ]] local QMAX = 8 local QVALMAX = 1000 local cfg = { on = true, gag = false, -- a copy by default; the MUD's own list still prints hide = true, -- put the panel away when you leave the shop qty = "1,5,10,25,50,100", } local QTYS = { 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100 } local widget = nil local view = "list" -- "list" | "settings" local items = {} local listing = false -- between the header and the footer local armed = nil -- the timer that disarms a list with no footer local vnum = 0 -- the room the current list came from local function trim(s) return (string.gsub(tostring(s or ""), "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1")) end --[[ Walked backwards rather than the usual gsub-until-no-more loop. That loop terminates on gsub's SECOND return, the replacement count — and this runtime is not a Lua VM. Written the idiomatic way, commas(0) spun forever the moment init() called render(), which locked the client on install before a single line of MUD output existed. Who's version does the same walk for the same reason. ]] local function commas(n) n = tonumber(n) if type(n) ~= "number" then return "0" end local s, out, c = tostring(math.floor(n)), "", 0 for i = string.len(s), 1, -1 do out = string.sub(s, i, i) .. out c = c + 1 if c % 3 == 0 and i > 1 then out = "," .. out end end return out end --[[ Read capture n. The guide says captures[1] is the first group. Our own S&D hedges by also checking captures[0], because arrays crossing the Lua/JS boundary arrive 0-indexed and nobody wrote down which side of that line this one lands on. The wildcards table sidesteps it entirely — it is keyed by the STRING "1", so there is no index base to get wrong. Try that first, then both bases. Getting this wrong costs a shop row parsed one column out, which reads as a price where a level should be and would happily buy the wrong thing. ]] local function cap(c, w, n) if type(w) == "table" and type(w[tostring(n)]) == "string" then return w[tostring(n)] end if type(c) == "table" then if type(c[n]) == "string" then return c[n] end if type(c[n - 1]) == "string" then return c[n - 1] end end return "" end local function esc(s) s = tostring(s or "") s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&") s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<") s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">") s = string.gsub(s, '"', """) return s end --- -- persistence --- --[[ saveTable is wiped when a plugin is removed and re-added, so the same blob goes into a world variable as well — those survive. Whichever is there on load wins, table first. ]] local function save_cfg() saveTable("aw_shop", cfg) pcall(function() setVariable(VAR, '{"on":' .. (cfg.on and "true" or "false") .. ',"gag":' .. (cfg.gag and "true" or "false") .. ',"hide":' .. (cfg.hide and "true" or "false") .. ',"qty":"' .. cfg.qty .. '"}') end) end --- -- quantity presets --- --[[ Whatever survives being a positive whole number, in the order you wrote them, deduped and capped. A bad list falls back to one button rather than none, so the panel is never a shop you can look at and not buy from. Second return is everything thrown away and why. Dropping a negative quietly is how you end up typing '/shop qty 1,5,-10' and believing you have three buttons — the panel would show two and never say which one it disagreed with. Nothing here truncates in silence. ]] local function set_qtys(spec) local out, seen, bad = {}, {}, {} for word in string.gmatch(tostring(spec or ""), "[^,%s]+") do local raw = tonumber(word) local n = raw and math.floor(raw) or nil if not n then table.insert(bad, word .. " (not a number)") elseif n < 0 then table.insert(bad, word .. " (negative)") elseif n == 0 then table.insert(bad, word .. " (zero)") elseif n > QVALMAX then table.insert(bad, word .. " (over " .. QVALMAX .. ")") elseif seen[n] then table.insert(bad, word .. " (already listed)") elseif #out >= QMAX then table.insert(bad, word .. " (only " .. QMAX .. " fit)") else seen[n] = true table.insert(out, n) end end if #out == 0 then out = { 1 } end QTYS = out return out, bad end --- -- capture --- --[[ Aardwolf paints item names, and the colour carries meaning — the bonus-loot bracket tier, and shop items that are quest or clan gear. Read it off the line rather than deciding for ourselves what an item should look like. parseAnsiText gives back segments with a hex colour each; the item name is the tail of the line, so the last coloured segment is the one that describes it. Anything that isn't a #rrggbb is dropped rather than trusted — this string ends up in a generated CSS rule. ]] local function colour_of(raw) if type(raw) ~= "string" or raw == "" then return nil end local ok, segs = pcall(parseAnsiText, raw) if not ok or type(segs) ~= "table" then return nil end local hex = nil for _, seg in pairs(segs) do if type(seg) == "table" and type(seg.color) == "string" then local c = string.match(seg.color, "^#%x%x%x%x%x%x$") if c and string.lower(c) ~= "#000000" then hex = c end end end return hex end --[[ Which room we're standing in, or 0 when the MUD hasn't said. Only used to notice you've walked out of the shop. A 0 never matches a real vnum, so an unknown room simply leaves the panel up rather than closing it on a guess. ]] local function room_now() for _, name in ipairs({ "room.info", "Room.Info" }) do local d = getGMCPData(name) if type(d) == "table" and tonumber(d.num) then return tonumber(d.num) end end return 0 end local function stop_listing() listing = false if armed then pcall(removeTimer, armed) armed = nil end end local render -- forward: the triggers below call it, and a forward -- reference here would silently resolve to a nil global local function on_head() if not cfg.on then return end items = {} stop_listing() listing = true vnum = room_now() -- a list with no footer would otherwise leave this armed for the session armed = addTimer(10000, function() stop_listing() render() end) showWidget(widget) render() if cfg.gag then return false end end local function on_row(c, line, w, raw) if not (cfg.on and listing) then return end local item = trim(cap(c, w, 5)) if item == "" then return end table.insert(items, { num = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1)) or 0, lvl = tonumber(cap(c, w, 2)) or 0, price = tonumber((string.gsub(cap(c, w, 3), ",", ""))) or 0, qty = trim(cap(c, w, 4)), item = item, col = colour_of(raw), }) if cfg.gag then return false end end local function on_foot() if not (cfg.on and listing) then return end stop_listing() render() if cfg.gag then return false end end --- -- paint --- local CSS_HEAD = [[ \n", seen end render = function() if not widget then return end local bar = '' .. commas(#items) .. ' for sale' .. '' .. '
settings
' .. '
' .. '×
' local css, cls = css_for(items) local body if view == "settings" then body = '
Capture
' .. '
' .. '
' .. (cfg.on and "on" or "off") .. '
' .. '
' .. 'hide output
' .. '
' .. 'close on leave
' .. '
' .. '
Type list in a shop. Hide output keeps ' .. 'the MUD\'s own list out of the terminal so only this panel shows it. ' .. 'Close on leave puts the panel away when you walk out — turn it ' .. 'off to keep a list up while you go and fetch the gold for it.
' .. '
Buy buttons
' .. '
' .. '' .. '
' .. '
Up to ' .. QMAX .. ' of them, each at most ' .. commas(QVALMAX) .. '. There is no confirmation on a buy, so the biggest ' .. 'button should still be a quantity you could mean.
' else body = "" if #items == 0 then body = '
Nothing listed — type list in a shop
' end for i, e in ipairs(items) do local qs = "" for _, q in ipairs(QTYS) do qs = qs .. '
' .. q .. '
' end body = body .. '
' .. '' .. e.lvl .. '' .. '' .. esc(e.item) .. '' .. (e.qty ~= "---" and ('x' .. esc(e.qty) .. '') or "") .. '' .. commas(e.price) .. '' .. '
' .. qs .. '
' .. '
' end end --[[ Say what a click does, where you'll see it before you click. There is no confirmation step and there shouldn't be one — a shop list you have to confirm twice is slower than typing 'buy 3' — but it should never be a surprise either. ]] local foot = (view == "list" and #items > 0) and '
the name appraises — the numbers buy, with no confirmation
' or "" setWidgetProperty(widget, "content", css .. '
' .. bar .. '
' .. '
' .. body .. '
' .. foot .. '
') end --- -- buying --- -- the row index, not the shop's number local function buy(i, qty) local e = items[tonumber(i) or 0] if not e then return end qty = math.floor(tonumber(qty) or 1) --[[ Belt and braces on the way out: the buttons can only carry what set_qtys allowed, but '/shop buy' takes a number off the command line and this is the last place before it becomes a purchase. ]] if qty < 1 then qty = 1 end if qty > QVALMAX then utilprint(TAG .. "$R" .. qty .. " is more than " .. commas(QVALMAX) .. " — not sending it.$w") return end -- 'buy 1 3' and 'buy 3' are the same thing; send the shorter one if qty > 1 then send("buy " .. qty .. " " .. e.num) else send("buy " .. e.num) end end --[[ Appraise is the only way to see what a shop item actually does, and it costs nothing — which is why it's on the name. The click you'll make by accident, on the item you were reading, is the one that spends no gold. ]] local function appraise(i) local e = items[tonumber(i) or 0] if not e then return end send("appraise " .. e.num) end --- -- setup --- function init() widget = createWidget({ type = "html", name = "shop", title = "Shop", position = { x = 560, y = 140 }, size = { width = 520, height = 420 }, visible = false, }) local saved = loadTable("aw_shop") if type(saved) ~= "table" then local ok, raw = pcall(function() return getVariable(VAR) end) if ok and type(raw) == "string" and raw ~= "" then local dok, data = pcall(json.decode, raw) if dok and type(data) == "table" then saved = data end end end if type(saved) == "table" then if saved.on == false then cfg.on = false end if saved.gag == true then cfg.gag = true end if saved.hide == false then cfg.hide = false end if type(saved.qty) == "string" and saved.qty ~= "" then cfg.qty = saved.qty end end set_qtys(cfg.qty) save_cfg() --[[ Triggers rather than onLine, because a trigger callback returning false gags the line and still runs — which is the whole job here. Comms does its gagging in onLine for the opposite reason: a line dropped there fires no triggers at all, so its captures had to live in the same pass. Nothing else needs to see shop rows, so this side of that trade is free. Regex is JavaScript flavour, and opting in is required — the default matcher is substring, which would match none of this. ]] addTrigger("^Num\\s+Level\\s+Price\\s+Qty\\s+Item\\s*$", on_head, { type = "regex" }) addTrigger("^\\s*(\\d+)\\s+(\\d+)\\s+([\\d,]+)\\s+(---|\\d+)\\s+(\\S.*?)\\s*$", on_row, { type = "regex" }) addTrigger("^(?:Quantity '---' means unlimited supply\\.|To see the stats of an item in the store, use 'Appraise '\\.)$", on_foot, { type = "regex" }) registerWidgetEvent(widget, "action", function(data) if type(data) ~= "table" then return end local act = tostring(data.action or "") local arg = tostring(data.data or "") if act == "buy" then local i, q = string.match(arg, "^(%d+),(%d+)$") if i then buy(tonumber(i), tonumber(q)) end return elseif act == "appraise" then appraise(tonumber(arg)) return elseif act == "close" then hideWidget(widget) return elseif act == "view" then view = (view == "settings") and "list" or "settings" elseif act == "on" then cfg.on = not cfg.on save_cfg() elseif act == "gag" then cfg.gag = not cfg.gag save_cfg() elseif act == "autohide" then cfg.hide = not cfg.hide save_cfg() end render() end) registerWidgetEvent(widget, "submit", function(data) if type(data) ~= "table" then return end local f = data.formData if type(f) ~= "table" then return end local got, bad = set_qtys(tostring(f.q or "")) cfg.qty = table.concat(got, ",") save_cfg() render() utilprint(TAG .. "buy buttons are now " .. table.concat(got, ", ") .. ".") if #bad > 0 then utilprint(TAG .. "$Rignored: " .. table.concat(bad, ", ") .. "$w") end end) render() registerCommand("shop", function(args) local a = args if type(a) == "table" then a = table.concat(a, " ") end a = trim(a) local verb, rest = string.match(a, "^(%S*)%s*(.*)$") verb = string.lower(verb or "") rest = trim(rest) if verb == "" or verb == "show" then showWidget(widget) elseif verb == "hide" then hideWidget(widget) elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then cfg.on = (verb == "on") save_cfg() render() utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.on and "'list' is copied to the panel." or "main window only.")) elseif verb == "gag" then cfg.gag = not cfg.gag save_cfg() render() utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.gag and "panel only — the list is hidden from the main window." or "the list prints in both places.")) elseif verb == "autohide" or verb == "keep" then cfg.hide = (verb == "autohide") save_cfg() render() utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.hide and "the panel closes when you leave the shop." or "the panel stays up until you close it.")) elseif verb == "qty" then if rest == "" then utilprint(TAG .. "buy buttons are " .. table.concat(QTYS, ", ") .. ". '/shop qty 1,5,10' to change, '/shop qty reset' for the default.") return end if string.lower(rest) == "reset" then rest = "1,5,10,25,50,100" end local got, bad = set_qtys(rest) cfg.qty = table.concat(got, ",") save_cfg() render() utilprint(TAG .. "buy buttons are now " .. table.concat(got, ", ") .. ".") if #bad > 0 then utilprint(TAG .. "$Rignored: " .. table.concat(bad, ", ") .. "$w") end elseif verb == "buy" then local n, q = string.match(rest, "^(%d+)%s*(%d*)$") if not n then utilprint(TAG .. "$Rusage: /shop buy [how many]$w") else buy(tonumber(n), tonumber(q)) end elseif verb == "appraise" or verb == "app" then local n = tonumber(rest) if not n then utilprint(TAG .. "$Rusage: /shop appraise $w") else appraise(n) end elseif verb == "clear" then items = {} render() utilprint(TAG .. "cleared.") else utilprint(TAG .. "shop stock in a panel.") utilprint("$w /shop show the panel") utilprint("$w /shop hide put it away") utilprint("$w /shop on | off copy 'list' to the panel, or don't") utilprint("$w /shop gag hide the list from the main window") utilprint("$w /shop autohide | keep close the panel when you leave, or don't") utilprint("$w /shop qty which buy buttons a row carries, e.g. 1,5,10") utilprint("$w /shop buy [n] same as clicking that row's number") utilprint("$w /shop appraise same as clicking the name; costs nothing") utilprint("$w /shop clear empty it") utilprint(TAG .. "state: " .. (cfg.on and "on" or "off") .. ", " .. (cfg.gag and "panel only" or "printed in both") .. ", " .. (cfg.hide and "closes on leave" or "stays up") .. ", buttons " .. table.concat(QTYS, ", ") .. ", " .. #items .. " item(s) listed.") end end, "shop stock in a panel; click a row to buy from it") --[[ Core owns Core.Supports.Set and builds the union from these declarations. Sending our own would REPLACE Aardwolf's record of every other plugin's subscriptions, including the room package the built-in mapper runs on. Room is wanted for one thing: noticing you've left. ]] broadcastPlugin("aw-gmcp", "Room") --[[ The panel is a popup. It appears when a list arrives and goes away when you walk out of the shop, because at that point it describes stock you can no longer buy — and a stale shop list you CAN still click is worse than no panel at all. Tied to the room changing rather than to a timer: how long you spend reading a shop list is not something a countdown can know. ]] local function left_shop() if not cfg.hide then return end local now = room_now() if now == 0 or vnum == 0 or now == vnum then return end vnum = 0 items = {} stop_listing() hideWidget(widget) render() end onGMCPUpdate("room.info", left_shop) onGMCPUpdate("Room.Info", left_shop) end
